notes: hook = full voiceover line. short = on-screen text, <=70 chars. asset names the real Split Index screen that carries the frame; asset_status says whether it has been captured. image_query is the stock fallback and is null wherever stock would undercut a hook that pays off on a number. Asset fields verified against the live app on 2026-09-06 by walking splitindex.co.uk while logged in.

asset_status_values.confirmed: a capture of this exact screen exists — shoot it
asset_status_values.needs_capture: the screen exists in the app but has not been captured yet
asset_status_values.blocked: cannot be captured from a real account as the hook is written — see asset_note
asset_status_values.stock: no app screen applies; use image_query

hooks.hook: Classified by pace, 100% of your runs look easy. Classified by heart rate, 6% are.
hooks.short: By pace: 100% easy. By heart rate: 6%.
hooks.frame: The finding card itself — 'PACE-VS-HR-DISCREPANCY' — with 100% and 6% pulled large.
hooks.asset: Hybrid Plan > Diagnostic > finding 4 (PACE-VS-HR-DISCREPANCY): 'Classified by pace, 100% of running looks easy; classified by heart rate, only 6% is. The paces are fine and the efforts are not - this is the grey zone, and pace-based classification cannot see it.' Also the 'Easy-running fraction 6% — grey-zone risk, by heart rate' row.
hooks.asset_note: Hook rewritten to the real numbers. 100% vs 6% is far more brutal than the 31% I invented, and it is the product's own sentence.
hooks.mechanic: accuses the viewer of something they cannot disprove without opening the app
hooks.usp: HR-primary intensity classification; emits a finding when pace and HR disagree by >25pp
hooks.next_beat: That gap has a name. It's why you've plateaued for eight months.

hooks.hook: I ran a slow 10k on purpose. My 5k prediction moved by 18 seconds. Not 8 minutes.
hooks.short: Slow 10k. My 5k prediction moved 18 seconds.
hooks.frame: Big number 18:00 -> 18:18, crossed-out '26:00' ghosted behind it.
hooks.asset: Analytics > Stored Predictions > RUNNING 5K card ('18:52', '26 sessions of evidence')
hooks.mechanic: concrete number contradicting an expectation — viewers wait to see how
hooks.usp: asymmetric memory predictions: faster session pulls 55% of the gap, slower nudges 4%
hooks.next_beat: Hard days prove fitness. Easy days hold it. Most apps average them and call it maths.

hooks.hook: I jogged slower to score higher. It docked me 1.6 points.
hooks.short: I jogged slower to score higher. It docked me.
hooks.frame: Score ticking 9.18 -> 7.54 in red while the pace number gets slower.
hooks.asset: The Engine > Endurance HQ session history — the 4:55/km run scoring 82.5 directly above the 9:00/km run scoring 69.7
hooks.asset_note: Strongest asset in the set: the hook is proven by two adjacent rows of real logged data, no mockup needed.
hooks.mechanic: claimed exploit — viewers stay to see whether it worked
hooks.usp: HR-efficiency gated by pace, so a slow low-HR effort earns no unearned bonus
hooks.next_beat: It knows the difference between getting fitter and just going slower.

hooks.hook: Your gym app gave you 847 points last night. Ask it where that number came from.
hooks.short: Your app gave you 847 points. Ask it why.
hooks.frame: Generic glowing '+847 PTS' badge shattering into DOTS 405 / IPF GL 83 / Age-graded 71%.
hooks.asset: Analytics > DOTS & IPF GL card — 319.8 and 65.3 side by side, 456.8 kg total
hooks.asset_note: Earlier flag withdrawn — the two DOTS figures are correct and deliberate, not a bug. The feed shows that SESSION's own SBD total (a bench-only session, 128kg) while Analytics shows the best-ever SBD total (456.8kg); same formula, different totals, verified numerically at bodyweight 78.05kg (128kg->89.6, 456.8kg->319.7, against 89.5 and 319.8 on screen). calculateOverallDotsGl in strength/overall-dots-gl.ts documents the split and the user feedback behind it. Shoot the Analytics card: it is the profile-level number an athlete would defend. Do not put the feed figure in the same frame without saying it is one session — the feed labels it plainly 'DOTS' with no session qualifier, so side by side they look contradictory to a viewer who does not know the distinction.
hooks.mechanic: names an enemy the viewer already half-distrusts
hooks.usp: DOTS, IPF GL and published age-graded standards — defensible, on separate scales by design
hooks.next_beat: These are the numbers federations actually use. Yours has been made up.

hooks.hook: Squat 180. Run an 18:40 5k. Which one of those is actually better? Nobody could tell you. Until now.
hooks.short: Squat 180. Run 18:40. Which is better?
hooks.frame: Two numbers on opposite sides, question mark between, collapsing into one 0-1000 index.
hooks.asset: Landing hero — LIFT HEAVY / RUN FAR with 70.8 SPLIT INDEX between 72.4 STRENGTH and 69.1 RUNNING
hooks.mechanic: poses a question hybrid athletes have never had answered
hooks.usp: The Lab and The Engine on one 0-1000 ruler, blended into a ranked Split Index
hooks.next_beat: Both scored on the same scale. One number. And a leaderboard that ranks it.

hooks.hook: This injury showed up in my data three weeks before it showed up in my leg.
hooks.short: This injury showed up in my data 3 weeks early.
hooks.frame: The Injury Risk trio pulled large — 51/95 Danger, 3.42x baseline, ACWR 2.23 — then the ACWR trend curve crossing into the red band.
hooks.asset: Analytics > Recovery & Injury Risk on the demo account (@demo_masters_hybrid) — INJURY RISK INDEX 51/95 Danger, RELATIVE RISK 3.42x vs baseline, ACWR 2.23, above the line 'Keep this week under ~426 AU (currently 730) to return to optimal.' The ACWR TREND chart underneath shows the curve crossing into the red band.
hooks.asset_note: CAPTURED on the live app, and the rendered figures are NOT the ones estimated from the database. A duration-weighted estimate gave ACWR 1.72 / 2.15x / index 32; the app computes load as TRIMP (duration x heart-rate intensity), so the real screen reads 2.23 / 3.42x / 51. Trust the screen. Rewrite the scripted line to 3.4x rather than the '2.1x baseline' it currently claims — the true number is more dramatic anyway. 'Keep this week under ~426 AU (currently 730)' is the strongest next_beat available and is on screen verbatim. Shoot on the demo account only; the founder's correctly reads Optimal at 0.92.
hooks.mechanic: fear plus a specific timeline; viewers want to see the warning
hooks.usp: Injury Risk Index from acute:chronic workload against your own baseline
hooks.next_beat: 'Keep this week under 426 AU. You're at 730.' That's a warning you can act on.

hooks.hook: Every race predictor uses the same fatigue number for you as for an Olympian. 1.06. Mine is 1.158.
hooks.short: Race predictors use 1.06 for everyone. Mine is 1.158.
hooks.frame: '1.06' stamped identically across a wall of runner silhouettes; one changes.
hooks.asset: Hybrid Plan > Diagnostic > finding 1 (ENDURANCE-LIMITED): 'Fatigue-resistance exponent k=1.158 vs population 1.06. This athlete fades faster than typical as distance rises.' Plus the 'Fatigue resistance (k) 1.158 — endurance-limited' row and 'Predicted 5k 17:49 — from your own maximal effort, using your own k'.
hooks.asset_note: The population-vs-personal comparison I scripted is literally on screen. Use the finding card.
hooks.mechanic: exposes a hidden assumption behind a tool the viewer has already used
hooks.usp: personal Riegel exponent k regressed from your own maximal efforts, driving a 1.5k-marathon ladder
hooks.next_beat: Mine's not 1.06. Yours isn't either. That's the difference between a guess and a prediction.

hooks.hook: This is the first training app that ever told me it didn't know something.
hooks.short: First app that ever told me it didn't know.
hooks.frame: Metric card reading 'Calibrating… 3/5 sessions logged' beside a completed one.
hooks.asset: Hybrid Plan > 'WHAT YOUR NEXT SESSIONS UNLOCK — Log a flat-out 400m. Your anaerobic speed reserve, which sets how much neuromuscular work belongs in your week.' Plus Diagnostic 'UNLOCK MORE' (3 items), 'Aerobic decoupling — needs a long run with per-km HR', and Interference's EARLY DATA badge.
hooks.asset_note: The unlock card is this hook's next_beat verbatim, already shipped. Strongest single asset in the set — and stronger still on the demo account (@demo_masters_hybrid), where the Hybrid Plan header reads 'Partly yours, partly population — 45% CONFIDENCE' above three named unlock prompts, each with a sentence saying what it would buy: 'Run a second maximal effort at a different distance', 'Log four easy runs with heart rate, run genuinely easily', 'Log both heavy sets (1-3 reps) and volume sets (6-12 reps)'. An app grading its own confidence at 45% and telling you how to raise it is the sharpest version of this hook there is.
hooks.mechanic: opposite of what viewers expect from an app ad — pattern interrupt
hooks.usp: every derived metric bound to the data supporting it; gaps become unlock prompts, not guesses
hooks.next_beat: 'A flat-out 400m unlocks your speed-reserve diagnosis.' It won't guess.

hooks.hook: Every session in my plan has a reason attached. If the engine can't say why, it isn't allowed to prescribe it.
hooks.short: Every session in my plan has a reason attached.
hooks.frame: A plan row expanding to reveal a plain-English finding underneath.
hooks.asset: Hybrid Plan header 'Built from 7 findings in your own logged history. Limiter: endurance.' > Diagnostic > 'What your data actually says — 7 findings', each tagged (ENDURANCE-LIMITED, LOW-VOLUME, GREY-ZONE, STALLED-LIFT...). Emphasis vector: 'Seven weights summing to 100%. Every session in your plan is allocated against these, and every one of them moved because of something in your own logged history.'
hooks.mechanic: an unusually strict rule — viewers stay for the example
hooks.usp: plans built from logged history; every session traceable to a named diagnostic finding
hooks.next_beat: Two people with the same 5k and the same free days get different plans.
hooks.asset_note: Also capture 'What we assumed' — the engine listing what it filled in rather than read is the same trust argument.

hooks.hook: You did 8 by 400 at 5k pace. Your app averaged in the rest and scored it like a jog.
hooks.short: You did 8x400. Your app scored it like a jog.
hooks.frame: Interval bar chart where the hard reps flatten into one grey line.
hooks.asset: no screen shows the work-piece pace — the scoring runs, nothing displays it
hooks.asset_note: Same shape as the age-graded hook. The mechanism ships: cardio/interval-scoring.ts converts work-piece pace via the rest ratio (intervalEquivalentPaceSecPerKm / fartlekEquivalentPaceSecPerKm) and it feeds the session score. But components/activities/interval-blocks.tsx is a logging INPUT only, and no result view renders work pace or contrasts it with the session average — so an athlete is never told their reps were scored rather than their session average, which is the entire claim of this hook. Needs a small display before it can be filmed.
hooks.mechanic: insults the viewer's hardest session of the week
hooks.usp: intervals and fartleks scored off work-piece pace with a rest-ratio conversion
hooks.next_beat: The reps get scored. The standing around doesn't.

hooks.hook: Your app says you bench 120. You benched 120 once. In March.
hooks.short: You bench 120? You benched 120 once. In March.
hooks.frame: 'BENCH 120kg' with a trophy, splitting into 'All-time 120 / Today 108'.
hooks.asset: Analytics > Adaptive 1RM — Bench Press 129.2 kg marked Falling, '97% of your best · 4.1 kg to go', 'Best 133.3 kg', under the header 'What your recent training says you could lift today, against the heaviest you have ever hit'
hooks.asset_note: That header is the hook already written. Show it, then the Falling bench.
hooks.mechanic: calls out a number the viewer is proud of and quietly suspects is stale
hooks.usp: three deliberate 1RM figures — all-time, current (which drops by design), and the scoring estimate
hooks.next_beat: A number that can only ever go up is a trophy. It isn't a training tool.

hooks.hook: You track squat, bench and deadlift. That's about 8% of what you actually do in the gym.
hooks.short: Squat, bench, deadlift. That's 8% of your training.
hooks.frame: Three lifts glowing, then twenty accessories lighting up around them, each with a 0-1000.
hooks.asset: Mobile > Adaptive 1RM scroll — Machine Chest Press 90.4, Seated Leg Curl 80.2, Preacher Curl 61.7, Tricep Pushdown 53.1, each with its own trend and likely range ('22 lifts' on the desktop header)
hooks.asset_note: Shoot as a scroll, not a still — the length of the list is the argument.
hooks.mechanic: an unflattering ratio the viewer can verify against their own logbook
hooks.usp: every lift scored on its own calibrated curve — a lateral raise and a pec deck aren't one multiplier
hooks.next_beat: Every set. Every accessory. Its own curve, its own score.

hooks.hook: A 62kg guy and a 100kg guy both bench 100. Your gym app says they're identical. They are not.
hooks.short: Two guys bench 100. Your app says they're identical.
hooks.frame: Two lifters, same barbell, same '100kg' — then two very different index scores.
hooks.asset_note: A constructed two-athlete comparison; no single app screen shows it. The social feed's 'bench: 128kg (1.64xBW)' chip works as the payoff card after the stock opener.
hooks.image_query: two weightlifters different body sizes bench press gym
hooks.mechanic: a fairness argument every lifter has had in a group chat
hooks.usp: allometric bodyweight scaling, so strength compares on a real curve not raw kilos
hooks.next_beat: Strength doesn't scale linearly with bodyweight. Your score shouldn't either.

hooks.hook: Most apps adjust for age by inflating your number. That's not a score. That's a sticker.
hooks.short: Apps 'adjust for age' by inflating you. That's a sticker.
hooks.frame: A number padded upward with confetti, hard-cut to the number holding still while the standard line drops.
hooks.asset: no screen renders the age adjustment — the engine computes it but nothing displays it
hooks.asset_note: Corrected 2026-09-06: the mechanism IS built, in both engines, and matches this hook's claim exactly. split-strength-engine.ts ageFactor() divides the ANCHOR (effectiveAnchor /= factor) so the athlete's own lift is never touched — literally 'the standard moves, not your number'. Cardio applies enduranceAgeGradeFactor() inside the pace score. What is missing is only the display: strength results carry the string 'age:NN xN.NNN standard (beta)' in appliedFactors, but the sole UI consumer (session-score-insights.tsx:198) reduces it to a boolean for a beta badge and never renders the string. So the claim is defensible and the frame is unshootable. Cheapest unblock is rendering that existing premium-gated string. Note the marketing site already claims age-graded standards (pricing-cta.tsx:27) while the product shows nothing — a consistency gap worth closing either way. Age factor remains beta and uncalibrated, so keep the copy on 'the standard moves', never on accuracy.
hooks.mechanic: reframes a feature the viewer thought was generous as patronising
hooks.usp: sex and age move the anchor you're judged against, never your own lift
hooks.next_beat: It doesn't change what you lifted. It changes what counts as good for you.

hooks.hook: Your 8-rep sets say your bench is 130. Your 3-rep sets say 118. That 12kg gap is the whole answer.
hooks.short: 8-rep sets say 130. 3-rep sets say 118. That gap is the answer.
hooks.frame: Two bars — 'VOLUME e1RM 130' and 'HEAVY e1RM 118' — with the gap highlighted.
hooks.asset: Mobile > bench logging screen — 100kg x 10 scoring 86.9 against 110kg x 6 scoring 85.4 and 120kg x 4, with EST 1RM 136 kg below
hooks.asset_note: Per-set scores differing across rep ranges on one screen is the gap, live. Stronger than the mocked two-bar frame.
hooks.mechanic: two numbers that shouldn't disagree; viewer wants to know which is lying
hooks.usp: rep-profile gap — positive means the muscle is built but not neurally expressed
hooks.next_beat: The muscle is there. You just can't express it yet. That's a six-week fix.

hooks.hook: Your squat isn't your weak lift. Your bench-to-squat ratio is, and it's been dragging your total for a year.
hooks.short: Your squat isn't the problem. Your bench-to-squat ratio is.
hooks.frame: Three lift bars with ratio bands overlaid; one falls visibly below its band.
hooks.asset: Hybrid Plan > Diagnostic > Strength profile on the demo account (@demo_masters_hybrid) — Squat 170kg (1.00x), Bench 93kg '0.55x your squat (typical 0.72x)', Deadlift 208kg (1.23x, typical 1.22x), then two rows reading 'Weak lift: bench' and 'Stalled lifts: bench'
hooks.asset_note: CAPTURED on the live app; rendered figures match the database exactly. Deadlift at 1.23x against a typical 1.22x is doing the work here — exactly one lift is out of proportion, so the panel names bench instead of reading as a generally imbalanced athlete. The weak-lift and stalled-lift rows sit adjacent, so hooks gym-16 and gym-18 can be shot from one frame. Founder's own account reads 'no weak lift, your lifts are in proportion'.
hooks.mechanic: promises a diagnosis of a plateau the viewer is already fighting
hooks.usp: lift ratios against published standards to name the lift limiting the total, plus ExRx accessory tiers
hooks.next_beat: It'll name the lift. Then it'll tell you what to do about it.

hooks.hook: You added 20kg to your pull-up. Your app logged 20kg. You actually moved 105.
hooks.short: You added 20kg to your pull-up. You moved 105.
hooks.frame: '+20kg' on screen, a bodyweight silhouette slides under it, number rolls to 105.
hooks.asset: Mobile > Adaptive 1RM — Weighted Pull Up 61.5 kg, 'At your all-time best', likely range 54.3-61.9 kg
hooks.asset_note: The Lab's explainer copy — added weight scored as what makes the movement equally hard for one rep, not bodyweight itself — is the payoff card.
hooks.mechanic: reveals a measurement error on a lift the viewer is proud of
hooks.usp: bodyweight-relative lifts scored off total load — full bodyweight for pull-ups and dips, a lower fraction for push-ups
hooks.next_beat: Added weight isn't the load. It never was.

hooks.hook: My bench hadn't moved in 11 weeks. It didn't tell me to push harder. It told me to stop benching.
hooks.short: 11 weeks stalled. It told me to stop benching.
hooks.frame: Flat e1RM line for 11 weeks, swap to a variation block, line breaks upward.
hooks.asset: Hybrid Plan > Diagnostic > finding 7 (STALLED-LIFT): 'Stalled over the last 12 weeks: bench. Progression rate below 0.15kg/week. A variation block is scheduled before returning to the competition lift.' Plus the 'Stalled lifts: bench' row.
hooks.asset_note: Detection AND prescription in one sentence — the half I thought was missing is there.
hooks.mechanic: advice is the opposite of what every gym video says
hooks.usp: stalled lifts detected from your own 12-week e1RM trend and routed into a variation block
hooks.next_beat: Stalled lifts don't need more effort. They need a different movement for a while.

hooks.hook: I took four months off. It didn't guilt-trip me. It just told me what I can lift today.
hooks.short: Four months off. It just told me what I can lift today.
hooks.frame: A gap in the calendar heatmap, then a clean current-1RM readout — no red, no streak banner.
hooks.asset: session history showing a real gap, then the current 1RM readout
hooks.asset_note: The clean-readout half can come from the live account. The gap half needs a seeded lapsed account — the live logbook has no four-month break. Keep image_query for the opening beat.
hooks.image_query: athlete returning to gym after break quiet determined
hooks.mechanic: speaks to the largest lapsed-user segment and is emotionally disarming
hooks.usp: current 1RM re-derived from logged sets every pass, so a return is measured not punished
hooks.next_beat: No streak shaming. It just recalculates.

hooks.hook: Your Tuesday run is taking something off Thursday's squat. Here's exactly how much, from your data, not a study.
hooks.short: Your Tuesday run is costing Thursday's squat. Here's how much.
hooks.frame: Bar chart of squat performance by days-since-cardio, one bar clearly depressed.
hooks.asset: Insights > Interference Radar on the demo account (@demo_masters_hybrid) — a large red '-5.8% CARDIO EFFICIENCY' beside 'Strength sessions cost you roughly 5.8% efficiency and +9bpm on running the next day.'
hooks.asset_note: Unblocked by scripts/seed-demo-athlete.ts and verified by calling fetchInterferenceReport directly. The day-1 bucket carries 10 samples at -5.8% EF and +9bpm; day-2 shows -10.8% off a single sample, so do not put day 2 on camera — one sample is not a finding. The summary sentence is the whole hook, so film the page rather than a mockup, and use its built-in 'Share as image' button. Founder's own account correctly reads 'no measurable interference' on 2 sessions.
hooks.mechanic: the interference debate is unresolved in every gym; promises a personal answer
hooks.usp: interference engine mines your own paired sessions both ways and refuses to claim an effect without enough data
hooks.next_beat: It works both ways. And it won't guess — it waits until it has your sessions.
